account: On Monday 28 June 2021 at about 4 pm a 65-year-old man with Alzheimer's disease left his home in Cergowa, south-east Poland. He had a stroke the previous day. Police and tracking dogs did not find him after a storm. On Tuesday 29 June the Bieszczady Mountain Rescue Service (GOPR Bieszczady) flew four drone flights. It ran SARUAV, software from University of Wrocław researchers that uses convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to find people in nadir aerial images, on 782 images. After 4 h 31 min of analysis the system detected him and returned his coordinates. He was lying unconscious in grass over two meters tall after more than 24 hours outdoors. GOPR rescuers carried him out and handed him to the ambulance service. The original study explicitly dates the search and rescue operation to June 29, 2021. Two authors from the Main School of Fire Service in Warsaw wrote in Sustainability in December 2021 that each use of SARUAV needs map data prepared for the area. In 2023, Texas A&M researchers wrote that SARUAV gives no details on its training data or model architecture. The developer's university reports that SARUAV located a second missing person in South Tyrol in August 2024, who had died, and that rescue services in Europe and Asia now use it.

display.answer: The case report in Remote Sensing and the University of Wrocław press release come from the developer's side. Three of the five case-report authors work for SARUAV Ltd., and one works for the Bieszczady Mountain Rescue Service. Three Polish news reports carry the account of GOPR Bieszczady. The 2021 Sustainability study restates the find from the makers' account, and its authors state that they did not test SARUAV themselves.

fields.account: On Monday 28 June 2021 at about 4 pm a 65-year-old man with Alzheimer's disease left his home in Cergowa, south-east Poland. He had a stroke the previous day. Police and tracking dogs did not find him after a storm. On Tuesday 29 June the Bieszczady Mountain Rescue Service (GOPR Bieszczady) flew four drone flights. It ran SARUAV, software from University of Wrocław researchers that uses convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to find people in nadir aerial images, on 782 images. After 4 h 31 min of analysis the system detected him and returned his coordinates. He was lying unconscious in grass over two meters tall after more than 24 hours outdoors. GOPR rescuers carried him out and handed him to the ambulance service. The original study explicitly dates the search and rescue operation to June 29, 2021. Two authors from the Main School of Fire Service in Warsaw wrote in Sustainability in December 2021 that each use of SARUAV needs map data prepared for the area. In 2023, Texas A&M researchers wrote that SARUAV gives no details on its training data or model architecture. The developer's university reports that SARUAV located a second missing person in South Tyrol in August 2024, who had died, and that rescue services in Europe and Asia now use it.
